title: Phase controlled spectral topology, dynamic stability and sensitivity in Non-Hermitian Cavity Magnonics
authors: Sachin Singh Bargahi, Rajeev Singh, Biswanath Bhoi
abstract: We theoretically investigate a non-Hermitian cavity-magnon platform in which coherent photonmagnon interactions and reservoir-mediated dissipative coupling interfere through a single externally tunable phase. We show that this interference phase provides a universal control parameter that continuously rotates the effective coupling between Hermitian and anti-Hermitian regimes, enabling dynamic transitions between level repulsion and level attraction without modifying intrinsic system parameters. The resulting phase-controlled non-Hermitian topology gives rise to exceptional points, linewidth engineering, and zero-damping conditions. Owing to the propagation-direction dependence of the dissipative interaction, the system further exhibits strong nonreciprocal transport and phase-tunable isolation arising from asymmetric hybridization of the cavity and magnon modes. Beyond its spectral and transport properties, we establish a direct connection between nonHermitian spectral topology and nonequilibrium population dynamics. The interference phase governs the stability of the hybrid modes, driving transitions between stable relaxation, critical slowing down near exceptional points, oscillatory energy exchange, and exponentially amplified dynamics. We further demonstrate that the same phase-controlled exceptional topology can be exploited for enhanced sensing, where the eigenvalue response exhibits the characteristic square-root scaling associated with exceptional-point physics. Our results provide a unified framework linking spectral topology, directional transport, dynamical stability, and sensing functionality through reservoirengineered interference in cavity magnonic systems.
summary: The paper theoretically explores controlling a coupled photon-magnon system using an external interference phase to manipulate its non-Hermitian spectral topology. This control allows for dynamic switching between different physical regimes and demonstrates that the resulting exceptional point physics can be exploited for superior sensing capabilities via square-root scaling of eigenvalue response.
main_problem: The study investigates how an externally tunable phase can control spectral topology, dynamic stability, and sensing capabilities in a non-Hermitian cavity-magnon system.
main_result: The interference phase acts as a universal control parameter, enabling dynamic transitions between different physical regimes (e.g., level repulsion to attraction) while demonstrating enhanced sensing via square-root scaling near exceptional points.
method: Theoretical analysis using non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and master equation formalisms to derive time evolution equations for system operators.
model_or_system: The platform is a coupled photon-magnon system in a microwave cavity, modeled by an effective Hamiltonian incorporating coherent coupling ($g$) and reservoir-mediated dissipative coupling controlled by an interference phase ($\Theta+\Phi$).
key_observables: Exceptional points (EPs), linewidth engineering, nonreciprocal transport ratios ($S_{21}/S_{12}$), dynamic stability (eigenvalue real parts $	ext{Re}(\lambda)$), and sensing responsivity $S$.
important_parameters: The interference phase ($\Theta+\Phi$), coupling strengths ($g, \Gamma$), detunings ($\delta_p, \delta_m$), and external perturbation strength ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA) and assumes steady-state or harmonic time dependence for spectral calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing transitions between coupling regimes, population dynamics over time for various phases, and eigenvalue splitting ($\Delta\lambda$) scaling near EPs.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (incorporating phase control) to analyzing spectral properties (EPs, level repulsion/attraction), then extending this analysis to dynamic stability (population evolution) and finally applying it to sensing applications using perturbation theory.
why_interesting: This work provides a comprehensive framework linking fundamental concepts of non-Hermitian physics—such as EPs and directional transport—to practical quantum technologies like enhanced sensing, all tunable via phase control in solid-state magnonics.
